pr_title: ao_openal: Fix null pointer dereference when creating OpenAL context
pr_body:
When the monitor goes to sleep, the OpenAL context was not properly handled, resulting in a null pointer dereference and a crash. This fix ensures that the OpenAL context is created and set correctly before proceeding. This avoids the crash under these conditions.

Fixes: #15648
Also fixes #[8307](https://github.com/SubtitleEdit/subtitleedit/issues/8307) of Subtitle Edit that utilizes Libmpv

Afterwards the important log part looks like this (can be compared to the log in #15648):

[ 108.517][d][ao/wasapi] Find device ''
[ 108.520][v][ao/wasapi] No device specified. Selecting default.
[ 108.534][v][ao/wasapi] Selecting device '{4d7dd748-07de-421c-9960-81369cb0b289}' (42 FHD_LCD-TV (NVIDIA High Definition Audio))
[ 108.534][v][ao/wasapi] Monitoring changes in device {0.0.0.00000000}.{4d7dd748-07de-421c-9960-81369cb0b289}
[ 108.540][d][ao/wasapi] Init wasapi thread
[ 108.540][d][ao/wasapi] Activating pAudioClient interface
[ 108.540][d][ao/wasapi] Probing formats
[ 108.548][v][ao/wasapi] Trying stereo float (32/32 bits) @ 48000hz (shared) -> AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_INVALIDATED (0x88890004)
[ 108.548][e][ao/wasapi] Error finding shared mode format: AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_INVALIDATED (0x88890004)
[ 108.548][d][ao/wasapi] Thread shutdown
[ 108.548][d][ao/wasapi] Uninit wasapi
[ 108.548][d][ao/wasapi] Thread uninit done
[ 108.548][d][ao/wasapi] Thread return
[ 108.548][d][ao/wasapi] Uninit wasapi done
[ 108.548][v][ao] Trying audio driver 'openal'
[ 108.548][v][ao/openal] requested format: 48000 Hz, stereo channels, floatp
[ 108.581][w][ao/openal] Direct channels aren't supported by this version of OpenAL
[ 108.581][f][ao/openal] Failed to create OpenAL context
[ 108.581][v][ao] Trying audio driver 'sdl'
...

The newly added check prevents LibMPV from crashing and LibMPV proceeds normally now..

Logfile with the fix in place:
[output.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18310571/output.txt)

issue_context.title: Libmpv crashes when monitors are going to sleep
issue_context.body:
### mpv Information

```bash
mpv v0.39.0-572-g4e8452ae Copyright © 2000-2025 mpv/MPlayer/mplayer2 projects
built on Jan  3 2025 12:04:15
libplacebo version: v7.350.0 (v7.349.0-30-g056b852-dirty)
FFmpeg version: N-118219-g551041e38
FFmpeg library versions:
libavcodec      61.28.100
libavdevice     61.4.100
libavfilter     10.6.101
libavformat     61.9.102
libavutil       59.53.100
libswresample   5.4.100
libswscale      8.13.100
```


### Other Information

```text
- Windows version: [Version 10.0.22631.4460]
- GPU model, driver and version: Nvidia Geforce RTX 3060, Driver 566.14
- Source of mpv: https://github.com/zhongfly/mpv-winbuild/releases
- Latest known working version: /
- Issue started after the following happened: /
```


### Reproduction Steps

1. Have two monitors connected to your system that report a sound output like "NVIDIA High Definition Audio"
2. Disable all other audio output devices via Windows settings so that only those with "NVIDIA HIgh Definition Audio" are available to select.
3. For testing set the timer to turn off the display to 1 minute in the power plan settings.
4. Open a video and pause it.
5. Minimize the player.
6. Let the monitors go to sleep.
7. Wake the system up. LibMPV is not anymore in the taskbar.

When looking at the log you find the following:

[  76.851][d][ao/wasapi] Find device ''
[  76.855][v][ao/wasapi] No device specified. Selecting default.
[  76.868][v][ao/wasapi] Selecting device '{16177f6c-268d-46d2-a53a-840a579be6a4}' (2460G4 (NVIDIA High Definition Audio))
[  76.868][v][ao/wasapi] Monitoring changes in device {0.0.0.00000000}.{16177f6c-268d-46d2-a53a-840a579be6a4}
[  76.875][d][ao/wasapi] Init wasapi thread
[  76.875][d][ao/wasapi] Activating pAudioClient interface
[  76.875][d][ao/wasapi] Probing formats
[  76.885][v][ao/wasapi] Trying stereo float (32/32 bits) @ 48000hz (shared) -> AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_INVALIDATED (0x88890004)
[  76.885][e][ao/wasapi] Error finding shared mode format: AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_INVALIDATED (0x88890004)
[  76.885][d][ao/wasapi] Thread shutdown
[  76.885][d][ao/wasapi] Uninit wasapi
[  76.885][d][ao/wasapi] Thread uninit done
[  76.885][d][ao/wasapi] Thread return
[  76.885][d][ao/wasapi] Uninit wasapi done
[  76.885][v][ao] Trying audio driver 'openal'
[  76.885][v][ao/openal] requested format: 48000 Hz, stereo channels, floatp
[  76.923][w][ao/openal] Direct channels aren't supported by this version of OpenAL

The monitors going to sleep triggers the audio device change but it tries switching to the other NVIDIA High Definition Audio Device that is also no longer available. Then it crashes in the OpenAL script (as seen later in the backtrace).

I could only reproduce this bug on my system running a NVIDIA graphics card. On my Intel Laptop this crash does not occur. Here the log reports the following:

[  66.330][d][ao/wasapi] Find device ''
[  66.336][e][ao/wasapi] There are no playback devices available
[  66.336][d][ao/wasapi] Uninit wasapi
[  66.336][d][ao/wasapi] Uninit wasapi done
[  66.336][v][ao] Trying audio driver 'openal'
[  66.336][v][ao/openal] requested format: 48000 Hz, stereo channels, floatp
[  66.356][f][ao/openal] could not open device
[  66.356][v][ao] Trying audio driver 'sdl'

Here occurs no fallback to a default device that is no longer available.

### Expected Behavior

Libmpv should handle this case and should continue to run normally.

### Actual Behavior

Libmpv crashes.
